supporting_evidence.summary: significant deviations in scope [all services]: currencyservice_latency-50 z=561.58 (2807.9%); currencyservice_latency-90 z=376.03 (4022.7%); frontend_latency-90 z=356.8 (1784.0%); checkoutservice_latency-50 z=286.16 (1452.5%)
traces for currencyservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.11->0.11ms (1.01x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 4.12->204.27ms (49.52x), errors 0.0->0.0

alternatives_rejected.why: Own-span self-time is unchanged at 0.11ms (1.01x) while caller-observed time rose 4.12->204.27ms. CPU saturation would slow its own processing, so the added time is in the network path (E2).
Its latency-50 z=286 is well below currencyservice's z=561. It calls currencyservice, whose inbound latency rose 49.5x, so checkoutservice's slowness is inherited (E1, E2).

Frontend latency-90 (z=356.8) is the top of the call chain and is explained by the downstream currencyservice delay. Its deviation is smaller than currencyservice's latency-50 and latency-90 (E1, E2).

proposed_fix.description: Inspect the currencyservice pod's network path for an injected delay (for example a tc/netem qdisc on its interface) and remove it. If the delay persists, roll out a fresh currencyservice pod. Then confirm that inbound p50 returns to about 4ms and that checkoutservice and frontend latencies recover.
